one_line: A cooperative escape-room game where human and AI inhabit asymmetric views and must coordinate to escape.
what_it_does: Presents a shared puzzle world in which the human sees visual glyphs and the agent accesses structured mechanisms/manual knowledge, requiring collaboration.
leverage_rationale: The stated design makes the structured agent surface the only way the agent touches the world, while deliberately exposing different information to human and agent; ordinary UI-driving is not a comparable substitute.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says human and AI perceive two different rooms and cannot escape alone.
About text reports 0% solo success for either side and 90% together across 20 runs.
Contact sheet visibly shows a purpose-built escape-room environment and robot/avatar interaction, though not readable tool calls.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent, highly intentional game premise and multiple in-world interaction states, but the submitted visual evidence does not clearly show a complete escape or end-to-end successful run.
execution_evidence: Three submitted frame sheets show intro, room overview, and repeated character/object interaction states.
About text describes multiple chambers, blackout, archive replay, finale lock, and ending shift report.
No transcript and no clearly legible completion state are provided.
impact_rationale: The cooperative puzzle directly creates a meaningful role for both a human player and an AI agent, with a credible entertainment and experimentation use case.
impact_evidence: The game is explicitly designed so neither participant can escape alone.
Reported 90% joint success indicates the collaboration is central to the intended experience.
creativity_rationale: Asymmetric perception and a deliberately indispensable human-agent escape-room relationship are a novel interaction model pursued with bespoke rooms, roles, and measured outcomes.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent receive different perceptual/action affordances.
The project frames coordination failure as deadlock and measures solo versus joint completion.
usability_note: The staged puzzle flow appears understandable, but evidence does not establish onboarding or accessibility details.
red_flags: No transcript; visible sheets do not expose readable tool calls or a clearly completed run.
standouts: WebMCP is structurally necessary rather than a convenience layer.
Strong human-agent asymmetry and quantified collaboration premise.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and creativity with a coherent product concept; advance despite incomplete end-to-end visual proof.

one_line: A theatrical fantasy-football draft-order randomizer presented as a live sports broadcast.
what_it_does: Lets a commissioner configure players and league presentation, then stages a chaotic race with commentary, replays, standings, and a verifiable randomized result.
leverage_rationale: Agents can configure players, colors, league name, audio, TV mode, and retrieve the draft board, making structured control useful; however, the same outcome is plausibly achievable through UI automation with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists agent controls for players, colors, league, audio, TV mode, and draft board.
The product's core value is the broadcast-style visualization rather than an agent-only capability.
execution_rationale: The description presents a complete, coherent event flow with many deliberate broadcast features, but there is no submitted video and the packet provides only packaging-level visual evidence.
execution_evidence: About text specifies setup, live race, standings, announcer updates, replays, Toilet Bowl, and verification.
Devpost facts report an alive demo and ten gallery images, but no video.
impact_rationale: Fantasy leagues have a clear recurring need for fair draft order, and turning it into a shared spectacle plausibly adds social value beyond a plain randomizer.
impact_evidence: The stated audience is fantasy-football leagues and draft-day groups.
The system addresses both randomization and communal entertainment, with a verifiable result.
creativity_rationale: The live fake-broadcast framing, chaotic runners, instant replays, and Toilet Bowl are a memorable synthesis for an otherwise mundane draft-order task.
creativity_evidence: Draft randomization is reimagined as a televised football event.
The packet describes custom broadcast network, crowd energy, penalties, mascots, and late-game drama.
usability_note: Configuration-to-live-event flow is concrete and TV-oriented, though unverified visually.
red_flags: No video submitted; execution is claimed from description and packaging.
standouts: Strong social entertainment framing for a routine league task.
Explicit verifiability addresses disputes about randomness.
advance_reason: Clear audience fit and unusually polished concept; WebMCP leverage is meaningful but not transformative.

one_line: A visual-fingerprint search and discovery interface for an archive of more than 7,000 music videos.
what_it_does: Combines visual-character search, graph connections, playback/queue controls, annotations, and an agent peer that watches and explains videos alongside the user.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools expose visual search, graph traversal with reasons, playback state, and queue operations that are difficult to express reliably through ordinary UI automation; the agent participates in discovery rather than merely answering chat.
leverage_evidence: About text lists 13 WebMCP tools including search_archive, find_by_look, follow_connection, play, queue_set, and now_playing.
Visual fingerprints enable natural-language discovery across motion, light, warmth, saturation, contrast, shot length, and cuts.
Agent and human share one screen and the agent explains why an item matters.
execution_rationale: The feature set and archive model are unusually specific and coherent, but there is no submitted video and the packet does not verify the live end-to-end experience.
execution_evidence: Description specifies archive scale, metadata, graph edges, playback, queue, annotations, and Discogs lookup.
Devpost facts report an alive demo and ten gallery images, but no video.
impact_rationale: Music-video researchers, archivists, curators, and fans have a real discovery problem that keyword search cannot solve well; visual retrieval and contextual connections address it directly.
impact_evidence: The stated audience includes archive and adjacent cultural-work users.
The product targets the concrete problem of finding a known-but-unnamable video.
creativity_rationale: Using visual fingerprints and a relationship graph to search music videos by felt visual character, with an agent as a peer curator, is a fresh and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Search by visual character avoids conventional keyword/sliders workflow.
The agent explains connection reasons and watches alongside the user rather than replacing the surface.
usability_note: The described shared-screen workflow is compelling, though the number of controls could create complexity.
red_flags: No video submitted; archive scale and tool behavior remain claimed.
standouts: Strong domain-specific data model and discovery interaction.
Agent collaboration is integrated into playback and curation.
advance_reason: High originality, audience fit, and substantial WebMCP delta despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: A collaborative evidence board for turning public comments into traceable, cited briefs.
what_it_does: Searches Regulations.gov comments, pins exact excerpts, lets an analyst verify or remove evidence, and uses the resulting shared state to prepare a cited brief.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects an agent to the analyst's live evidence board with structured search, pinning, and review state; this shared human verification loop is materially more reliable than scraping or generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly describes agent searches and pins, analyst verification/removal, and agent reading those decisions.
The workflow validates quotes against original records and excludes unreviewed evidence from exports.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and addresses traceability, but no frame sheets or video are submitted, so end-to-end completion and polish cannot be established.
execution_evidence: Description names pagination, quote validation, review gating, and cited brief generation.
Demo is reported alive, but gallery_images is 0 and no video is provided.
impact_rationale: Policy analysts and researchers face a real high-volume evidence-traceability problem, and the product directly preserves source links and human review.
impact_evidence: The stated use case is researching thousands of public comments.
The product keeps findings traceable and prevents unreviewed evidence from entering exports.
creativity_rationale: The shared evidence-board pattern and explicit human review boundary are a strong, domain-appropriate interaction design for agent-assisted public-comment research.
creativity_evidence: Agent and analyst operate on shared evidence state rather than a chat transcript.
Quote validation and review gating are built into the concept.
usability_note: The review-first flow should support trust, but there is no visual evidence to assess interaction friction.
red_flags: No images or video submitted; all execution claims are textual.
standouts: Clear high-value research audience and problem.
advance_reason: Excellent impact and leverage concept; advance with execution confidence reduced for absent visual evidence.

one_line: A guided, agent-ready career planning journey connecting degree progress to skills and opportunities.
what_it_does: Walks students through dependent choices about direction, role, priorities, academic route, workload, skill gaps, and experience while agents use structured planning tools.
leverage_rationale: The tool surface exposes typed career-path exploration and degree-plan simulation over real structured data, while consequential choices remain human-controlled; generic UI driving would be less precise and trustworthy.
leverage_evidence: About text reports 33 top-level WebMCP tools.
Examples include explore_career_path and simulate_degree_plan with schemas.
The student approves choices and the journey visibly narrows subsequent options.
execution_rationale: The nine-step journey and constraints are well specified and appear intentional, but there is no video and no gallery imagery, limiting proof of completion and polish.
execution_evidence: Description defines nine dependent steps and constraints such as prerequisite-safe terms and bounded skill gaps.
Alive demo and public repository are reported, but no video is submitted.
impact_rationale: Students have a real problem navigating degrees, skills, internships, scholarships, and competing priorities; constrained, explainable guidance is a strong fit.
impact_evidence: The packet identifies dashboard overload and unsupported chatbot advice as opposing failures.
The product keeps important decisions under student control and uses real degree/career relationships.
creativity_rationale: The one-supported-choice-at-a-time advising model and explicit agent/student division are a fresh synthesis beyond a generic career chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Dependent narrowing is designed to mimic a good advisor rather than expose a catalog.
Agent tools operate directly on planning capabilities while the student retains authority.
usability_note: Progressive narrowing should reduce overwhelm; actual usability is unverified without visual evidence.
red_flags: No video or gallery images; claimed nine-step completion cannot be checked.
standouts: Strong human-control boundary for consequential planning.
Concrete structured domain model rather than open-ended advice.
advance_reason: High impact with strong leverage and a thoughtful interaction model; advance while discounting execution confidence.

one_line: A crowd-flow rehearsal tool that lets event organisers test repairs before doors open.
what_it_does: Models event queues and bottlenecks, has an agent propose and stress-test safe changes, compares outcomes, and requires organiser approval before commitment.
leverage_rationale: The agent can generate, compare, and stress-test structured scenario changes against shared simulation state, while the human retains approval; this is more reliable than generic UI manipulation.
leverage_evidence: Workflow includes baseline rehearsal, several draft repairs, before/after comparison, disruption stress tests, and approval.
The agent is explicitly prevented from committing the final plan without organiser review.
execution_rationale: The stated simulation loop is coherent and safety-conscious, but there are no submitted frames or video, so the actual model and completed workflow are unverified.
execution_evidence: About text enumerates inputs, baseline metrics, repairs, stress testing, and approval.
Public repository and alive demo are reported; no gallery images or video.
impact_rationale: Event organisers have a concrete safety and operations problem, and rehearsing queues before a live crowd can prevent costly or dangerous failures.
impact_evidence: Use cases include concerts, college festivals, and conferences.
The tool targets registration, security, scanner failures, arrival surges, and stage timing.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-assisted what-if rehearsal with explicit human approval to event crowd operations is a useful and relatively distinctive interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The product treats an event plan as a scenario to stress-test rather than a static dashboard.
Disruption cases are part of the core loop, not an afterthought.
usability_note: The staged baseline/repair/approval workflow is sensible, but visual usability is unavailable.
red_flags: No visual evidence; simulation fidelity and actual comparison views are unknown.
standouts: Strong safety boundary and clear operational audience.
Stress testing makes the agent role substantive.
advance_reason: High practical impact and credible leverage; execution evidence is the main weakness.

one_line: A guided workflow that turns business automation ideas into ROI, readiness, and implementation plans.
what_it_does: Runs deterministic diagnostics, delegates interpretation to opportunity-analyst and solution-architect specialists, exposes results, and recalculates ROI from estimated operating costs.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools and specialist handoffs improve repeatability and inspectability, but the same planning outcome could be achieved by a capable agent with ordinary application access and the delta is not shown as indispensable.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five diagnostics and two specialist handoffs through WebMCP.
Financial calculations remain deterministic Python functions while the model interprets and plans.
Users can inspect results and approval points.
execution_rationale: The workflow is unusually well scoped, with deterministic calculations separated from local-model interpretation and explicit limitations, but no visual/video evidence demonstrates completion.
execution_evidence: Description specifies diagnostics, specialist roles, handoff, ROI recalculation, scenarios, and limitations.
Public repository, alive demo, and three frame sheets are reported, but images were not successfully available for full review.
impact_rationale: Businesses commonly need help deciding whether automation ideas are worth pursuing and whether they are ready; bounded ROI and readiness analysis addresses that planning gap.
impact_evidence: The stated problem is prioritizing AI opportunities and assessing data/process readiness.
The tool produces implementation phases and human approval points rather than claiming to execute enterprise actions.
creativity_rationale: The combination of deterministic diagnostics, two bounded AI specialists, and inspectable handoffs is a thoughtful synthesis, though the underlying business-planning category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Two specialist roles are chained with a recalculation loop.
Synthetic invoice and customer-support scenarios make the workflow concrete.
usability_note: A guided diagnostic sequence should be usable for nontechnical business users, but no visual proof is available.
red_flags: No transcript; visual frame review was unavailable after transient vision rate limiting.
Uses synthetic scenarios and does not connect to real ERP or invoice systems.
standouts: Clear separation of deterministic financial logic from model interpretation.
advance_reason: Credible, useful workflow with good execution claims; advance, but not as a top leverage entry.

one_line: A WebMCP-enabled workspace for manipulating and cleaning Excel and CSV files.
what_it_does: Aims to let users use an agent to understand and perform spreadsheet operations such as filtering, deduplication, and data cleaning.
leverage_rationale: Spreadsheet manipulation can benefit from structured commands, but the packet does not specify distinctive tools or shared-state behavior beyond the existing file-editing UI; generic agent automation likely achieves comparable results.
leverage_evidence: Description identifies ExcelJS, Next.js, shadcn, and WebMCP.
The stated motivation is automating common manual spreadsheet operations, not a demonstrated WebMCP-specific capability.
execution_rationale: The packet is extremely thin: a one-line pitch and broad motivation without workflow details, screenshots proving functionality, or video evidence.
execution_evidence: Only a short description and technology list are provided.
No video frame sheets and no gallery images are submitted.
impact_rationale: Spreadsheet cleaning and editing are common, real productivity needs, but the packet does not establish how much better this product is than existing tools or agents.
impact_evidence: The stated problem concerns recurring manual filtering, deduplication, and cleaning work.
A live demo and public repository are reported.
creativity_rationale: The category is useful but familiar, and the packet presents no distinctive interaction or novel angle beyond adding WebMCP to spreadsheet editing.
creativity_evidence: Pitch is simply ‘Manipulate and edit excel/csv files.’
No original workflow, audience specialization, or novel interaction is described.
usability_note: Likely familiar in concept, but no interface evidence supports a stronger assessment.
red_flags: No frames, video, or concrete tool/workflow description.
advance_reason: The problem is real, but WebMCP delta, originality, and execution are not evidenced sufficiently for advancement.

one_line: A shared watercolor studio where a human and AI agent paint along with Bob Ross lessons.
what_it_does: Provides separate synchronized lesson players, transcript, human and agent easels, WebGL watercolor simulation, physical-pigment mixing, episode palettes, and agent painting/video controls.
leverage_rationale: The agent has its own canvas and lesson state and can paint through structured tools while the human paints in parallel; ordinary UI driving would be unreliable for continuous synchronized creative collaboration.
leverage_evidence: About text lists tools for controlling video, reading captions, inspecting lessons, and painting on the agent canvas.
Human and agent each receive an independent easel and synchronized lesson context.
The agent is a co-creator with persistent visual output, not merely a chat layer.
execution_rationale: The scope is ambitious but internally coherent, with a detailed rendering and paint model plus synchronized lesson workflow; submitted frames support a substantial product claim, though no completion video is present.
execution_evidence: Description specifies WebGL2 canvas, pigment flow, drying, paper fibers, Kubelka–Munk blending, brushes, palettes, transcript, and two players.
Three frame sheets and three gallery images are reported.
No submitted video means the full paint-along loop is not demonstrated end-to-end.
impact_rationale: Painting learners and casual creative users have a clear desire for guided, low-pressure practice; a co-painting agent adds companionship and experimentation.
impact_evidence: The project targets people learning or painting along with a familiar instructional series.
Separate easels support participation rather than passive content consumption.
creativity_rationale: A synchronized human-agent paint-along with distinct canvases, watercolor simulation, and lesson-aware agent behavior is highly original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: The interaction model is parallel co-creation on separate easels.
Physical pigment simulation and lesson-specific color collection extend the concept beyond a generic drawing app.
usability_note: The studio metaphor and guided lesson should be approachable, though advanced controls may add complexity.
red_flags: No transcript and no video; full synchronization and agent painting behavior are not fully verified.
standouts: Exceptional creative ambition and memorable human-agent interaction.
Agent has a real canvas and creative agency.
advance_reason: One of the strongest concepts in the packet: high leverage, originality, and credible depth.

one_line: A WebMCP-native ideation canvas where founders combine sponsors, industries, and wild-card constraints.
what_it_does: Maintains a local board of typed idea elements, supports document ingestion, combination, SCAMPER expansion, idea listing, and Markdown export for human-agent collaboration.
leverage_rationale: Structured board tools and shared local state make agent contributions more precise than chat, but the same ideation outcome is possible with a general agent operating a canvas or document with some friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists list_palette, add_element, ingest_doc, combine, list_ideas, scamper, download_canvas, and reset_canvas tools.
Human and agent use the same board with localStorage state and typed categories.
Document ingestion enables the agent to add external idea material into the shared canvas.
execution_rationale: The concept and tool list are concrete, but the packet has no video and no frame sheets, and describes an intentionally simple client-only implementation with limited evidence of robustness.
execution_evidence: Description specifies board fields, interactions, exports, tools, and localStorage architecture.
Four gallery images are reported but no video or frame sheets.
impact_rationale: First-time founders and hackathon teams have a recognizable need for structured ideation, and combining constraints can produce useful prompts and directions.
impact_evidence: The stated audience is first-time founders and hackathon teams.
The board supports ingesting lists and exporting ideas in Markdown.
creativity_rationale: The three-lane combination canvas and live human-agent board are a fresh, playful ideation interaction, though ideation canvases are an established category.
creativity_evidence: Sponsors, Industries, and Wild Cards create a simple combinatorial mechanic.
SCAMPER is optional and layered onto the shared board rather than replacing it with chat.
usability_note: Simple lanes and color coding should be approachable; local-only persistence may limit reliability.
red_flags: No video or frame sheets; localStorage-only implementation may limit durability and collaboration beyond one browser.
Sparse project title/pitch wording suggests packaging polish is limited.
standouts: Playful constrained-combination mechanic suited to ideation.
advance_reason: Promising and coherent, but impact and execution evidence are modest and WebMCP is a meaningful rather than decisive delta.
